§2.3 The Hodge–Tate and de Rham specializations
§4 The A_inf-cohomology of Drinfeld symmetric spaces
§5 Integral p-adic étale cohomology of Drinfeld symmetric spaces

summary: The integral refinement of the companion paper's computation: for the Drinfeld symmetric space H^d_K = P^d_K ∖ (K-rational hyperplanes) and every i ≥ 0 there are compatible topological isomorphisms of G × G_K-modules H^i_ét(H^d_C,Z_p(i)) ≅ Sp^i(Z_p)^* and H^i_ét(H^d_C,F_p(i)) ≅ Sp^i(F_p)^*, where Sp^i is the generalized Steinberg representation of G = GL_{d+1}(K); in particular the integral cohomology is p-torsion free and everything vanishes above degree d. The obstacle is that the integral comparison theorems of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze and Česnavičius–Koshikawa — which for a proper semistable model deduce p-torsion freeness of the étale cohomology of the generic fibre from that of the de Rham cohomology of the model — are proved using properness, while the standard model of the Drinfeld space is not even quasi-compact. The way round is to compute the A_inf-cohomology instead: the technical theorem is a topological φ^{-1}-equivariant isomorphism H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) ≅ A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^*, and the integral étale answer follows from it through a formula of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze — a twisted Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → H^{i−1}(AΩ{i})/(1−φ^{-1}) → H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) → H^i(AΩ{i})^{φ^{-1}=1} → 0 — which needs no quasi-compactness, together with A_inf^{φ^{-1}=1} = Z_p and A_inf{1}/(1−φ^{-1}) = 0. The A_inf-cohomology itself is computed by building an A_inf-symbol map out of the pro-étale Kummer sequence and the twisted Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism, integrating those symbols against Z_p-valued measures on the space of (i+1)-tuples of hyperplanes — after Schneider–Stuhler and Iovita–Spiess, the Steinberg dual being the quotient of such distributions by the degenerate ones — and then proving that the resulting regulator is an isomorphism by derived Nakayama: both sides are derived ξ̃-complete and ξ̃-torsion free, and modulo ξ̃ the map becomes, through the Hodge–Tate specialisation and the acyclicity of the sheaves of logarithmic differentials on the standard model, the Hodge–Tate regulator that the companion paper had already computed.

items.name: The setting: the Drinfeld symmetric space, its standard model and the A_inf-side objects
items.statement: p is a prime, K a finite extension of Q_p, C the p-adic completion of an algebraic closure K̄, G_K = Gal(K̄/K). The Drinfeld symmetric space of dimension d over K is the rigid analytic variety H^d_K := P^d_K ∖ ∪_{H ∈ H} H, where H = P((K^{d+1})^*) ≅ P^d(K) is the space of K-rational hyperplanes in K^{d+1}; it carries an action of G = GL_{d+1}(K). X_{O_K} denotes the standard semistable formal model of H^d_K over O_K (Grosse-Klönne), 𝔛 := X_{O_K} ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, X := H^d_K ⊗̂_K C the rigid analytic generic fibre of 𝔛 and X_K = H^d_K. All completed tensor products in the paper are taken in the category of pro-discrete modules.
items.note: The same objects as in the companion paper PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20, which computed the rational answer; this paper refines it integrally.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (= Theorem 5.1): the integral and mod p étale cohomology of the Drinfeld symmetric space
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 there are compatible topological isomorphisms of G × G_K-modules H^i_ét(H^d_C, Z_p(i)) ≅ Sp_i(Z_p)^* and H^i_ét(H^d_C, F_p(i)) ≅ Sp_i(F_p)^*, compatible with the rational isomorphism H^i_ét(H^d_C,Q_p(i)) ≅ Sp_i(Z_p)^* ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p of the companion paper. In particular these groups vanish for i > d. Here Sp_i(Z_p) is the generalized Steinberg representation of G with the trivial G_K-action and Sp_i(Z_p)^* its Z_p-dual.
items.note: The main theorem. In particular the integral cohomology is p-torsion free, which is what makes the mod p statement follow from the integral one.

items.name: Remark 1.2: the history, the compactly supported computation, and the absence of Poincaré duality
items.statement: (i) For d = 1 and i = 1 the result is due to Drinfeld, with a shaky proof corrected in Fresnel–van der Put; see also Theorem 1.7 of the companion paper on the Drinfeld tower. (ii) Colmez–Dospinescu–Hauseux–Nizioł compute the étale cohomology with compact support of many p-adic period domains by methods that avoid p-adic Hodge theory, following Orlik's ℓ-adic computations and using Ext groups between mod p representations; for H^d_C the answer reads H^i_{ét,c}(H^d_C, Z/p^n) ≅ Sp_{2d−i}(Z/p^n)(d−i) as G × G_K-modules, for p ≥ 5. (iii) Hence étale cohomology and étale cohomology with compact support of H^d_C are in abstract duality H^i_{ét,c}(H^d_C,Z/p^n) ≅ H^{2d−i}_ét(H^d_C,Z/p^n)^*(−d); but there is no known Poincaré duality for spaces like H^d_C that would explain it, and computations with basic analytic spaces such as the unit ball show that there is no naive Poincaré duality for general p-adic rigid analytic spaces.
items.note: Part (i) is the third independent report of the defect in Drinfeld's ℓ = p proof (the two companion papers report it as well); part (iii) is recorded as a gap — the duality is observed, not proved, and must not be planned as a target.

items.name: Grosse-Klönne's acyclicity (1.3) and the ordinarity of the standard model
items.statement: For the standard semistable formal model X_{O_K} of H^d_K one has H^i(X_{O_K}, Ω^j_{X_{O_K}}) = 0 for all i ≥ 1 and j ≥ 0, where Ω^•_{X_{O_K}} is the logarithmic de Rham complex of X_{O_K} over O_K for the canonical log structures of X_{O_K} and O_K (Grosse-Klönne). One easily infers that X_{O_K} is ordinary in the usual sense. The strongest and easiest integral p-adic comparison theorems are available for ordinary varieties, but X_{O_K} is not quasi-compact, which is the obstacle to the usual strategy.
items.note: The same acyclicity that drives §6 of the companion paper; it is an item of the Drinfeld roadmap proposed there, and this paper is a second consumer.

items.name: The strategy: why properness is the obstacle, and how A_inf-cohomology removes it
items.statement: The syntomic method of the companion paper works only up to absolute constants and reduces the computation of H^i_ét(H^d_C,Q_p(i)) to the integral Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the special fibre, which was computed there and which also shows that the de Rham cohomology of X_{O_K} is p-torsion free. The results of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, adapted to the semistable case by Česnavičius–Koshikawa, show that for proper rigid analytic varieties with semistable reduction, p-torsion freeness of the de Rham cohomology of the model (equivalently of the integral Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the special fibre) implies p-torsion freeness of the p-adic étale cohomology of the generic fibre; combined with the rigidity of G-invariant lattices in Sp_i(Q_p) (Grosse-Klönne) this would give the main theorem — but those proofs rely on properness. The A_inf-cohomology, however, makes perfect sense without it, and a formula of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze relates p-adic étale cohomology to A_inf-cohomology even for non-quasi-compact varieties, which reduces the main theorem to a computation of A_inf-cohomology.
items.note: This is the conceptual content of the paper: the passage from a syntomic argument that only works up to constants to an A_inf argument that is exact, at the cost of having to compute the A_inf-cohomology of a non-quasi-compact space.

items.name: A_inf, the element μ and the Breuil–Kisin twist M{i}
items.statement: A_inf = W(O_C^♭) is Fontaine's ring associated with C. A compatible system (ζ_{p^n})_n of primitive p-power roots of unity gives ε ∈ O_C^♭ = lim←_{x ↦ x^p} O_C and hence μ = [ε] − 1 ∈ A_inf, and a modified (Breuil–Kisin) Tate twist M ↦ M{i} := M ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf{i} on A_inf-modules, where A_inf{1} := (1/μ)A_inf(1) ⊂ W(C^♭)(1) and A_inf{i} := A_inf{1}^{⊗i}. One writes ξ̃ = φ(μ)/μ.
items.note: AI.0 forms A_inf = W(O_C^♭) with its Frobenius and θ, defines μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{-1}(μ) and ξ̃ = φ(ξ), and proves the nonzerodivisor and completeness properties; the Breuil–Kisin twists are AI.2/AI.4 material. The paper is a consumer.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (= Theorem 4.1): the A_inf-cohomology of the Drinfeld symmetric space
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 there is a topological φ^{-1}-equivariant isomorphism of G × G_K-modules H^i_ét(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛{i}) ≅ A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp_i(Z_p)^*.
items.note: The technical heart. Theorem 1.1 follows from it together with the nearby-cycle description of p-adic étale cohomology in terms of AΩ.

items.name: The twisted Artin–Schreier exact sequence (1.5) computing p-adic étale cohomology from A_inf-cohomology
items.statement: There is an exact sequence 0 → H^{i−1}_ét(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛{i})/(1 − φ^{-1}) → H^i_ét(X, Z_p(i)) → H^i_ét(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛{i})^{φ^{-1}=1} → 0, a twisted version of the Artin–Schreier exact sequence; it is the description of p-adic nearby cycles in terms of AΩ due to Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, and it holds without any quasi-compactness hypothesis.
items.note: PR.4 names BMS2 §10 among its sources and requires the "truncation and nearby-cycle/logarithmic de Rham–Witt comparisons under BS22/BMS2's hypotheses"; the extraction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 routes its chapter-10 items there too. This paper is a consumer, and the remark that the formula needs no quasi-compactness — "especially remarkable due to its simplicity" — is the observation that makes the whole argument possible.

items.name: The proof of Theorem 1.4: the regulator, derived Nakayama, and the Hodge–Tate reduction
items.statement: Fix i and write M = H^i(𝔛, AΩ_𝔛{i}), an A_inf-module which is derived ξ̃-complete for ξ̃ = φ(μ)/μ. First, following Schneider–Stuhler and Iovita–Spiess, Sp_i(Z_p)^* is interpreted as a quotient of the space of Z_p-valued measures on H^{i+1}, which gives an étale regulator r_ét : Sp_i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) and hence a regulator r_inf : A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp_i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}). To prove that r_inf is an isomorphism one uses the derived Nakayama lemma: both sides being derived ξ̃-complete it suffices that r_inf ⊗^L Id_{A_inf/ξ̃} be a quasi-isomorphism. The Hodge–Tate specialisation of AΩ_𝔛 identifies H^i(AΩ_𝔛/ξ̃) with the twisted sheaf of i-th logarithmic differential forms on 𝔛, which are well controlled by the acyclicity (1.3); combined with the compatibility of the étale and Hodge–Tate Chern class maps this shows that the reduction of r_inf is isomorphic to the Hodge–Tate regulator r_HT : O_C ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp_i(Z_p)^* → H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛), which the companion paper proved to be an isomorphism. Along the way one shows that H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) is ξ̃-torsion free; since the domain is too, the naive reduction agrees with the derived one and the argument closes.
items.note: The derived Nakayama lemma plus a torsion-freeness statement is the whole architecture; the only geometric input is the acyclicity (1.3) and the companion paper's computation of the integral de Rham cohomology.

items.name: Theorem 5.1: the integral and mod p étale cohomology, assembled
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 there is a G × G_K-equivariant topological isomorphism r_ét : Sp_i(Z_p)^* ≅ H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)), compatible with the rational isomorphism of the companion paper, and a G × G_K-equivariant topological isomorphism Sp_i(F_p)^* ≅ H^i_ét(X,F_p(i)). For i = 0 the regulators are the identity on Z_p and F_p. For i > 0 one passes to pro-étale cohomology through H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) ≅ H^i_proét(X,Ẑ_p(i)), applies the exact sequence (5.2) and Theorem 4.1, and computes H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})^{φ^{-1}=1} ≅ (A_inf ⊗̂ Sp_i(Z_p)^*)^{φ^{-1}=1} ≅ A_inf^{φ^{-1}=1} ⊗̂ Sp_i(Z_p)^* ≅ Sp_i(Z_p)^* and H^{i−1}_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})/(1−φ^{-1}) ≅ (A_inf{1} ⊗̂ Sp_{i−1}(Z_p)^*)/(1−φ^{-1}) ≅ (A_inf{1}/(1−φ^{-1})) ⊗̂ Sp_{i−1}(Z_p)^* = 0; the mod p statement follows because Sp_i(F_p)^* ≅ Sp_i(Z_p)^* ⊗ F_p and, by the integral statement, H^i_ét(X,F_p(i)) ≅ H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) ⊗ F_p.
items.note: The two vanishing computations A_inf^{φ^{-1}=1} = Z_p and A_inf{1}/(1−φ^{-1}) = 0 are what make the Artin–Schreier sequence collapse to an isomorphism. As printed, the last tensor factor of the second chain is Sp_i(Z_p)^* where Sp_{i−1}(Z_p)^* is meant; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: Definition 2.1 and the properties of derived I-completeness, including the derived Nakayama lemma
items.statement: For a finitely generated ideal I of a ring A, an object M ∈ D(A) is derived I-complete if for every f ∈ I the homotopy limit of the tower (⋯ → M —f→ M —f→ M) vanishes. Then: a classically I-complete module is derived I-complete, and conversely if it is I-adically separated; the derived I-complete complexes form a full triangulated subcategory D_comp(A,I) ⊂ D(A), and the inclusion has a left adjoint M ↦ M̂, the derived I-completion (which is in general not holim_n(M ⊗^L_A A/I^n)); M is derived I-complete if and only if all its cohomology groups are; if I = (x_1,…,x_n) then derived I-completeness is equivalent to derived (x_i)-completeness for each i; Rf_* commutes with derived completions; and (derived Nakayama) a derived I-complete M is 0 if and only if M ⊗^L_A A/I ≃ 0.
items.locator: Definition 2.1 and §2.1.1, p. 4 (after the Stacks Project)
items.note: AI.1 opens by requiring a replete ringed topos and locally finitely generated J "as required in that section's opening assumptions … explicit hypotheses of the completion exports", i.e. it owns the derived-completion package of BMS1 §6.2. Derived Nakayama is the engine of §4 of this paper. Note that the same Stacks tag is cited for two logically independent statements here; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The Berthelot–Deligne–Ogus décalage functor Lη_f and its properties
items.statement: For a ring A and a non-zero-divisor f ∈ A there is a functor Lη_f : D(A) → D(A), not exact in general, with a functorial isomorphism H^i(Lη_f T) ≅ H^i(T)/H^i(T)[f]: choose a representative T^• with f-torsion-free terms and set η_f(T^•)^i = {x ∈ f^i T^i : dx ∈ f^{i+1}T^{i+1}} inside T^•[1/f]. The coordinate-free form of the cohomology formula is H^i(Lη_f T) ≅ (H^i(T)/H^i(T)[f]) ⊗_A (f^i). It commutes with truncations and with restriction of scalars, Lη_f Lη_g ≅ Lη_{fg}, it inverts f (Lη_f(T)[1/f] ≅ T[1/f]) and its reduction mod f is the Bockstein complex (H^*(T/f), β_f); it preserves distinguished triangles when the boundary maps H^i(M/f) → H^{i+1}(T/f) vanish, commutes with reduction mod g when H^*(T/f) has no g-torsion, preserves derived I-completeness (on a replete topos for an invertible ideal sheaf), and is lax symmetric monoidal. For T ∈ D^{[0,d]}(A) with H^0(T) f-torsion-free there are natural maps Lη_f(T) → T (the canonical map) and T → Lη_f(T) whose composites are multiplication by f^d.
items.note: AI.1 is exactly this stage: "construct eta_f on a termwise f-torsionfree complex inside its localization … Prove its cohomology formula removing f-torsion with the appropriate degree scaling, its natural transformation after localization, compatibility with composition in eligible elements, and its lax symmetric monoidal structure". The canonical map and the f^d factorisation are what §2.4 of this paper uses to compare AΩ with Rν_*A_inf. The paper cites the truncation property as [5, Cor. 6.5] in one place and [5, Lemma 6.5] in another; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: A_inf = W(O_C^♭) with ε, μ, ξ, the maps θ, θ_∞, θ̃, the element ξ̃, and their arithmetic
items.statement: O_C^♭ := lim_{x↦x^p} O_C ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} O_C/p is the tilt of O_C and C^♭ = Frac(O_C^♭) an algebraically closed field of characteristic p. A_inf := W(O_C^♭) with its Frobenius automorphism φ. A fixed compatible sequence (1,ζ_p,ζ_{p^2},…) of primitive p-power roots of unity gives ε ∈ O_C^♭ and one sets μ := [ε] − 1 and ξ := μ/φ^{-1}(μ) = ([ε]−1)/([ε^{1/p}]−1). The surjection O_C^♭ → O_C/p lifts to θ : A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ), which lifts further to θ_∞ : A_inf → W(O_C) with kernel (μ) (θ_∞ need not be surjective); the twisted map θ̃ := θφ^{-1} has kernel generated by ξ̃ := φ(ξ) = φ(μ)/μ = ([ε^p]−1)/([ε]−1), and θ̃(μ) = ζ_p − 1. Moreover ξ̃ ≡ p mod μ; A_inf and A_inf/p are domains with ξ, ξ̃, μ non-zero mod p, so (p,ξ), (p,ξ̃), (p,μ) and (ξ̃,μ) are regular sequences; and the ideals (p,ξ), (p,ξ̃), (ξ̃,μ) define the same topology on A_inf. All of this generalises with O_C replaced by an arbitrary perfectoid ring.
items.note: AI.0 forms A_inf = W(O_C^♭) with its Frobenius and θ, defines μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{-1}(μ) and ξ̃ = φ(ξ), records θ and θ̃ = θ∘φ^{-1} with their kernels, and proves the nonzerodivisor, completeness and torsion properties — this item verbatim. The congruence ξ ≡ p mod φ^{-1}(μ) is what makes the injectivity argument of Lemma 2.11 work.

items.name: The Breuil–Kisin twists O_C{1}, A_inf{1} and M{i}, with the generator ω and the maps φ^{±1}, θ̃
items.statement: The chosen roots of unity give a basis ζ of Z_p(1). By Fontaine's theorem the O_C-module O_C{1} := T_p(Ω^1_{O_C/Z_p}) is free of rank 1, and dlog : μ_{p^∞} → Ω^1_{O_C/Z_p} induces an injection dlog : O_C(1) → O_C{1} with dlog(ζ) = (dlog ζ_{p^n})_{n≥1}; O_C{1} is generated by ω := (1/(ζ_p−1))·dlog(ζ), so the annihilator of coker(dlog) is (ζ_p − 1), and for an O_C-module M one sets M{1} := M ⊗_{O_C} O_C{1}, with a{1} = a·ω in O_C{1}. On the A_inf side A_inf{1} := (1/μ)A_inf(1) ⊂ W(C^♭)(1) and a{1} := (1/μ)a(1); since φ(μ) = ξ̃μ, φ induces an isomorphism A_inf{1} ≅ (1/ξ̃)A_inf{1} whose inverse restricts to φ^{-1} : A_inf{1} → A_inf{1}, and θ̃ : A_inf{1} → O_C{1} sends a{1} to θ(φ^{-1}(a))·ω. For an A_inf-module M, M{i} := M ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf{1}^{⊗i}, i ∈ Z, and θ̃ induces θ̃ : M{1} → (M/ξ̃){1}.
items.note: AI.0 fixes the period-ring normalisation and AI.4 the Breuil–Kisin twists in the Hodge–Tate reduction ("identifying its cohomology sheaves with differential forms and BK twists"). The explicit generator ω and the identity θ̃(μx{1}) = (ζ_p−1)x{1} are the normalisation that §3.2 of this paper needs to match the A_inf and Hodge–Tate symbols. As printed, a{1} = (1/μ)a(1) is said to lie in A_inf(1) rather than A_inf{1}; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The pro-étale period sheaf A_inf,X and the complexes AΩ_𝔛 = Lη_μ Rν_*A_inf,X and Ω̃_𝔛 = Lη_{ζ_p−1} Rν_*Ô^+_X
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be a flat p-adic formal scheme, locally of finite type over O_C, whose generic fibre X is a smooth adic space over C, and let ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét be the natural morphism of sites. A_inf,X := (W(lim_φ O^+_X/p))^ is a sheaf of complexes of A_inf-modules on X_proét, the hat denoting derived p-adic completion; it behaves as if naively defined, since for an affinoid perfectoid U = Spa(R,R^+) one has H^0(U,A_inf) = A_inf(R^+) and [m^♭]·H^i(U,A_inf) = 0 for i > 0, and it carries a Frobenius φ which is a quasi-isomorphism and a map θ : A_inf → Ô^+_X := lim_n O^+_X/p^n compatible with θ : A_inf → O_C. One sets AΩ_𝔛 := Lη_μ(Rν_*A_inf,X) ∈ D^{≥0}(𝔛_ét,A_inf), a commutative ring object and an A_inf-algebra because Lη_μ and Rν_* are lax symmetric monoidal, and Ω̃_𝔛 := Lη_{ζ_p−1}(Rν_*Ô^+_X) ∈ D^{≥0}(𝔛_ét), a commutative O_𝔛-algebra object.
items.note: AI.3 constructs the completed integral structure sheaf, its tilt and the Witt sheaf A_inf,X on the pro-étale site with Scholze's corrected covers, and defines AΩ = Lη_μ Rν_* A_inf,X with its Frobenius and multiplication — this item verbatim. That the μ-torsion-freeness of A_inf gives H^0(T)[μ] = 0 is what makes can_0 bijective in the proof of Theorem 2.9.

items.name: Small algebras, framings, the Galois setup (R̂, Δ, A_∞, R_∞, Γ) and almost purity
items.statement: A formally smooth O_C-algebra R with Spf(R) connected together with an étale map A := O_C{T_1^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}} → R is called a small algebra with framing A → R. R̄ denotes the normalisation of R in the maximal pro-finite-étale extension of R[1/p], R̂ its (perfectoid) p-adic completion and Δ := Gal(R̄[1/p]/R[1/p]); A_∞ := O_C{T_1^{±1/p^∞},…,T_d^{±1/p^∞}} and R_∞ := R ⊗̂_A A_∞, so that Γ := Gal(R_∞/R) ≅ Z_p(1)^d = ⊕_i Z_p γ_i with γ_i(T_i^{1/p^n}) = ζ_{p^n}T_i^{1/p^n} and γ_i(T_j^{1/p^n}) = T_j^{1/p^n} for j ≠ i, all group cohomology being continuous. By Faltings' almost purity theorem RΓ(Γ,R_∞) → RΓ(Δ,R̂) is an almost quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: AI.3 says to "build a toric perfectoid cover of a small framed affine, compute its continuous group cochains using the canonical general cohomology carrier, and prove the almost purity comparison", which is this item. §3.2 of this paper reduces to exactly this local situation with d = 1.

items.name: Theorems 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze): the Hodge–Tate sheaves of Ω̃ in the smooth case
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be smooth over O_C. (Theorem 2.2) For every i there is a natural isomorphism of O_𝔛-modules H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ Ω^i_{𝔛/O_C}{−i}. (Theorem 2.3) For R a small algebra with a framing, X = Sp(R[1/p]) and 𝔛 = Spf(R): the natural maps Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ(Γ,R_∞) → Lη_{ζ_p−1}RΓ(X_proét,Ô^+_X) → RΓ(𝔛,Ω̃_𝔛) are quasi-isomorphisms; writing Ω̃_R for any of them, Ω̃_R ⊗_R O_𝔛 → Ω̃_𝔛 is a quasi-isomorphism; and for a formally étale map R → S of small algebras, Ω̃_R ⊗^L_R S → Ω̃_S is a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently H^i(Ω̃_R) ≅ H^i(Γ,R_∞)/H^i(Γ,R_∞)[ζ_p−1] ≅ H^i(Γ,R), the last being a decompletion result. (Theorem 2.4) For R a small algebra there is a natural R-linear isomorphism H^1(Ω̃_R) ≅ Ω^1_{R/O_C}{−1}, and the cup products induce ∧^i H^1(Ω̃_R) ≅ H^i(Ω̃_R), hence H^i(Ω̃_R) ≅ Ω^i_{R/O_C}{−i}; the difficulty is to define these isomorphisms canonically, independently of coordinates. Explicitly, after reduction to A = O_C{T^{±1}} the twisted map α : Ω^1_{R/O_C} ≅ H^1(Ω̃_R){1} → (ζ_p−1)H^1(Γ,R_∞){1} satisfies α(dT/T) = (γ ↦ 1 ⊗ dlog(ζ_γ)) = (γ ↦ (ζ_p−1) ⊗ (1/(ζ_p−1))dlog(ζ_γ)), where ζ_{γ,n} := γ(T^{1/p^n})/T^{1/p^n}.
items.locator: Theorems 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 with the explicit description of α, §2.3.1, pp. 7–8
items.note: AI.4 proves the Hodge–Tate reduction of AΩ along θ̃ identifying the cohomology sheaves with differential forms and Breuil–Kisin twists; AI.3 supplies the local framed computation. The explicit formula for α(dT/T) is what §3.2 of this paper compares with Scholze's isomorphism.

items.name: Semistable formal schemes over O_C, their canonical log structure and logarithmic differentials
items.statement: 𝔛 is semistable over O_C if locally for the étale topology 𝔛 = Spf(R) with R admitting an étale morphism of O_C-algebras A := O_C{T_0,…,T_r,T_{r+1}^{±1},…,T_d^{±1}}/(T_0⋯T_r − p^q) → R for some d ≥ 0, r ∈ {0,…,d} and a rational q > 0 (a fixed embedding p^Q ⊂ C). O_C carries the log structure O_C ∖ {0} → O_C and 𝔛 the canonical log structure, the sheafification of the subpresheaf O_{𝔛,ét} ∩ (O_{𝔛,ét}[1/p])^*; Ω^1_{𝔛/O_C} is the finite locally free O_𝔛-module of logarithmic differentials, with its exterior powers and the log de Rham complex, and 𝔛^sm denotes the smooth locus.
items.note: AI.6 extends AI.3–5 "to the precise semistable formal models of Česnavičius–Koshikawa: proper flat formal models over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue field, base changed to O_C, with their standard semistable charts and divisorial log structures" — the same class, except that this paper's models are not proper, which is the point of the Part II route.

items.name: Theorem 2.5 and Remark 2.6 (Česnavičius–Koshikawa): the Hodge–Tate sheaves of Ω̃ in the semistable case
items.statement: Let 𝔛 be semistable over O_C with its canonical log structure. There is a unique O_{𝔛,ét}-module isomorphism H^1(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ Ω^1_{𝔛/O_C}{−1} whose restriction to 𝔛^sm is the isomorphism of Theorem 2.2, and the cup product ∧^i H^1(Ω̃_𝔛) → H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) is an isomorphism, so H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ Ω^i_{𝔛/O_C}{−i} naturally. The construction (Remark 2.6): the completed-cotangent-complex argument of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze gives a map Ω^{1,cl}_{𝔛/O_C}{−1} → R^1ν_*Ô^+_X from classical (non-logarithmic) differentials, whose composite with the projection to H^1(Ω̃_𝔛) restricts to an isomorphism Ω^1_{𝔛^sm/O_C}{−1} ≅ (ζ_p−1)H^1(Ω̃_𝔛)|_{𝔛^sm}; since H^1(Ω̃_𝔛) is a vector bundle one can divide that map by ζ_p − 1 and extend the result to the isomorphism asserted. The cup products are induced by the product maps H^1(T)^{⊗i} → H^i(T) for T = Rν_*Ô^+_X, using H^i(Ω̃_𝔛) ≅ H^i(T)/H^i(T)[ζ_p−1].
items.note: AI.6 says the logarithmic extension "is additional proof work, not a consequence of appending log to AΩ", which is exactly the content of Česnavičius–Koshikawa. Their paper has no extraction of its own in the atlas, so it is listed in the prerequisites.

items.name: Theorem 2.8 and the specialisation maps: AΩ_𝔛/ξ̃ ≅ Ω̃_𝔛, AΩ_𝔛/ξ ≅ Ω^•_{𝔛/O_C}, and derived ξ̃-completeness
items.statement: For 𝔛 semistable over O_C the map θ̃ = θφ^{-1} : A_inf,X → Ô^+_X is surjective with kernel generated by the non-zero-divisor ξ̃, so it gives a quasi-isomorphism Rν_*A_inf,X ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃} O_C ≅ Rν_*Ô^+_X, and since θ̃(μ) = ζ_p − 1 it induces a morphism AΩ_𝔛/ξ̃ := AΩ_𝔛 ⊗^L_{A_inf,θ̃} O_C → Ω̃_𝔛. Theorem 2.8 (Česnavičius–Koshikawa): (1) that morphism is a quasi-isomorphism (the Hodge–Tate specialisation); (2) there is a natural quasi-isomorphism AΩ_𝔛/ξ ≅ Ω^•_{𝔛/O_C} onto the logarithmic de Rham complex (the de Rham specialisation); (3) AΩ_𝔛 is derived ξ̃-complete, hence so are RΓ_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛) and its cohomology groups. On cohomology one defines ι̃_HT : AΩ_𝔛 → AΩ_𝔛/ξ̃ ≅ Ω̃_𝔛 and ι_HT : H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛) → H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_{𝔛/O_C}{−i}) as ι̃_HT followed by the edge map of the spectral sequence H^s_ét(𝔛,H^t(Ω̃_𝔛)) ⇒ H^{s+t}_ét(𝔛,Ω̃_𝔛) and the isomorphism of Theorem 2.5; similarly ι̃_dR : AΩ_𝔛 → AΩ_𝔛/ξ ≅ Ω^•_{𝔛/O_C} and ι_dR : H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛) → H^i_dR(𝔛).
items.locator: Theorem 2.8 and the two specialisation maps, §2.3.2, p. 9
items.note: AI.6 is asked to "prove derived comparisons with log de Rham, Hyodo–Kato/log crystalline, A_cris and étale cohomology" for semistable models, and AI.4 the smooth Hodge–Tate and de Rham distinction. Derived ξ̃-completeness is what licenses the derived Nakayama argument of §4, and ι_HT is the map Proposition 3.3 is about.

items.name: The sheaf Ẑ_p on the pro-étale site and the vanishing of the derived limits
items.statement: On X_proét one defines Ẑ_p := lim_n Z/p^nZ, and R^i lim_n Z/p^nZ = 0 for i > 0 (Scholze); this is not tautological, since X_proét is not a replete topos.
items.note: A1 builds the pro-étale site with Scholze's corrected covering definition; the failure of repleteness and the vanishing of the derived limits belong with it. The same vanishing is used again in §3 for the pro-étale Kummer sequence.

items.name: The operators ψ_i = ξ^iφ^{-1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛 and the twisted operator 1 − φ^{-1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛{i}
items.statement: There is an endomorphism ξ^iφ^{-1} of τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛, defined as τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛 ≅ Lη_μτ^{≤i}Rν_*A_inf —φ^{-1}→ Lη_{φ^{-1}(μ)}τ^{≤i}Rν_*A_inf —ξ^i→ Lη_ξLη_{φ^{-1}(μ)}τ^{≤i}Rν_*A_inf = τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛, the last equality because Lη_ξLη_{φ^{-1}(μ)} = Lη_{ξφ^{-1}(μ)} = Lη_μ; it is an endomorphism in D(𝔛_ét) but not an A_inf-linear one. The isomorphisms μ^{-i} : τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛 ≅ τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛{i} conjugate 1 − ξ^iφ^{-1} into an operator 1 − φ^{-1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛{i}, using ξ^iφ^{-1}(μ^i x) = μ^iφ^{-1}(x). One writes ψ_i := ξ^iφ^{-1}, also as the evident endomorphism of T := Rν_*A_inf, and the two are compatible with the canonical map can : AΩ_𝔛 → T; M_i := H^i(T).
items.note: The conjugation by μ^{-i} is what turns the arithmetic operator ξ^iφ^{-1} into the geometric 1 − φ^{-1} of the Artin–Schreier sequence, and it is the reason the twist A_inf{i} rather than A_inf(i) appears in the answer. Routed with the Part II: PrismaticCohomology PR.4 owns the resulting nearby-cycle formula, not this construction.

items.name: Theorem 2.9 and its proof beyond the good-reduction case: p-adic nearby cycles as Frobenius fixed points for any flat formal model
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over C and 𝔛 a flat formal model of X — not necessarily semistable and not necessarily quasi-compact — and let i ≥ 0. There is a natural quasi-isomorphism γ : τ^{≤i}Rν_*Ẑ_p(i) ≅ τ^{≤i}[τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛{i} —1−φ^{-1}→ τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛{i}] onto the homotopy fibre, whence the exact sequence 0 → H^{i−1}_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})/(1−φ^{-1}) → H^i_proét(X,Ẑ_p(i)) → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})^{φ^{-1}=1} → 0, Galois equivariantly if 𝔛 is defined over O_K. Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze prove this in the good reduction case; the paper shows the proof goes through for an arbitrary flat formal model. Applying Rν_* to Lemma 2.10(b) gives the triangle Rν_*Ẑ_p —μ^i→ T —1−ψ_i→ T and hence τ^{≤i}Rν_*Ẑ_p ≅ τ^{≤i}T^{ψ_i=1}, so it suffices to compare τ^{≤i}(τ^{≤i}AΩ_𝔛)^{ψ_i=1} with τ^{≤i}T^{ψ_i=1} along the canonical map; by homological algebra this holds provided 1 − ψ_i acts bijectively on ker and coker of can_j : H^j(AΩ_𝔛) → H^j(T) for j < i, bijectively on the kernel and injectively on the cokernel for j = i. For j = 0, can_0 is bijective because H^0(AΩ_𝔛) ≅ H^0(T)/H^0(T)[μ] and A_inf is μ-torsion free; for j > 0 the isomorphism μ^j : M_j/M_j[μ] ≅ H^j(AΩ_𝔛) puts can_j in the exact sequence 0 → M_j[μ] → M_j[μ^j] → H^j(AΩ_𝔛) → M_j → M_j/μ^j → 0, compatible with the operators 1 − ψ_{i−j}, 1 − ψ_{i−j}, 1 − ψ_i, 1 − ψ_i, 1 − ψ_i, so that Lemma 2.11 applies.
items.note: The statement is Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze's (chapter 10, after Morrow), and the atlas plans it at PrismaticCohomology PR.4; what is this paper's own is that the proof needs neither properness nor quasi-compactness of 𝔛 — which is precisely what lets the Drinfeld symmetric space be treated — so the item is routed with the Part II.

items.name: Lemmas 2.10 and 2.11: the Artin–Schreier description of Ẑ_p and the bijectivity of 1 − ψ_l
items.statement: Lemma 2.10: for i ≥ j the map 1 − ψ_i : A_inf/μ^j → A_inf/μ^j is a quasi-isomorphism (Morrow), and μ^i : Ẑ_p ≅ [A_inf —1−ψ_i→ A_inf] is a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of sheaves on X_proét — proved from the derived p-complete Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism Ẑ_p ≅ [A_inf —1−φ^{-1}→ A_inf] together with the fact that (μ^i,μ^i) is a morphism of complexes, since ξ^iφ^{-1}(μ^i x) = μ^iφ^{-1}(x), whose cone is acyclic by the first part. Lemma 2.11 (Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze): for j ≥ 1, i ≥ 0 and M_i = H^i(Rν_*A_inf), the operator 1 − ψ_{l+j} is bijective on M_i/μ^j for l > 0 and injective for l = 0; 1 − ψ_l is bijective on M_i[μ^j] for l > 0 and surjective for l = 0; and 1 − ψ_l is bijective on M_i[μ^j]/M_i[μ] for all l ≥ 0. The injectivity on M_i[μ^j] for l > 0 reduces by induction to j = 1, where μx = 0 and x = ξ^lφ^{-1}(x) give, using ξ ≡ p mod φ^{-1}(μ) and that φ^{-1}(μ) kills φ^{-1}(x), the equation (1 − pξ^{l−1}φ^{-1})(x) = 0, whence x = 0 because 1 − pξ^{l−1}φ^{-1} is an automorphism of the derived p-complete module M_i; the rest follows from the map of triangles T —μ^j→ T → T/μ^j and Lemma 2.10.
items.note: Lemma 2.11 is quoted as Lemma 10.5 of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze's second paper and Lemma 2.10 rests on Morrow's "p-adic vanishing cycles as Frobenius-fixed points"; PR.4 names BMS2 §10 among its sources, and the extraction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 routes its chapter-10 fixed-point items there. The diagram in the proof of Lemma 2.10(b) prints the cone with μ^j where μ^i is meant; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The topology convention: naive (quotient) topology on cohomology, not the refined quasi-abelian one
items.statement: Integrally one works in the category of pro-discrete modules and rationally in locally convex topological Q_p-vector spaces, as in §2.2 of the companion paper; but in this paper the cohomology groups carry the naive topology, i.e. the quotient topology, rather than being the refined cohomology groups (written H̃ in the companion paper) taken in the derived category of pro-discrete modules.
items.note: Worth keeping: the two papers make different topological choices, so a statement about H̃ in the companion paper is not literally a statement about the groups here. The quasi-abelian machinery is the Part II proposed by the companion extraction under LocallyAnalyticDistributions.

items.name: The pro-étale and A_inf symbol maps r_proét and r_inf
items.statement: Let X be a smooth adic space over C and 𝔛 a flat p-adic formal model of X over O_C, with ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét the projection. For i ≥ 1 one constructs compatible continuous symbol maps r_proét : O(X)^{*,⊗i} → H^i_proét(X,Ẑ_p(i)) and r_inf : O(X)^{*,⊗i} → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}). For i = 1 they come from maps of sheaves c^{proét}_1 : τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1]) → τ^{≤1}(Rν_*Ẑ_p(1)) and c^{inf}_1 : τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1]) → τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1}, on applying H^1_ét(𝔛,−) and using H^1_ét(𝔛,τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1])) ≅ H^1_ét(𝔛,Rν_*G_m[−1]) = H^0_ét(𝔛,Rν_*G_m) ≅ O(X)^*; for i ≥ 1 one takes cup products, x_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ x_i ↦ r_*(x_1) ∪ ⋯ ∪ r_*(x_i).
items.note: The A_inf member of the family of Chern class maps that §7 of the companion paper builds (crystalline, Hyodo–Kato, logarithmic de Rham–Witt, de Rham and overconvergent); nothing in the atlas has Chern classes of units into AΩ.

items.name: The Kummer sequence on the pro-étale site and the twisted Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: The first map of (3.2) uses the Kummer exact sequence on X_proét, 0 → Ẑ_p(1) → lim←_{x ↦ x^p} G_m → G_m → 0, obtained by passing to the limit in 0 → μ_{p^n} → G_m —p^n→ G_m → 0 and using the vanishing of R^1 lim←_n Z/p^n (Scholze, Prop. 8.2); projecting to 𝔛_ét gives the Chern class map c^{proét}_1 : Rν_*G_m[−1] → Rν_*(Ẑ_p(1)). The second uses in addition the twisted Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism on X_proét, Ẑ_p(1) —γ→≅ [A_inf{1} —1−φ^{-1}→ A_inf{1}], where γ is defined by x(1) ↦ μx{1}; pushing down gives β : τ^{≤1}Rν_*Ẑ_p(1) → τ^{≤1}Rν_*A_inf{1}, while Theorem 2.9 gives γ : τ^{≤1}Rν_*Ẑ_p(1) → τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1}. The two are compatible through τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1} → τ^{≤1}Rν_*A_inf{1}, and the composite τ^{≤1}Rν_*Ẑ_p(1) —γ→ τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1} —1−φ^{-1}→ τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1} is zero. The A_inf symbol map is then c^{inf}_1 := γ ∘ c^{proét}_1.
items.note: The vanishing of the composite with 1 − φ^{-1} is what makes the symbols land in the φ^{-1}-fixed part, which is the term the Artin–Schreier sequence identifies with étale cohomology.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate symbol map and the canonical log structure
items.statement: Let X_{O_K} be a semistable formal scheme over O_K with sheaf of monoids M defining the log structure and M^gp its group completion. This log structure is canonical in Berkovich's terminology: M(U) = {x ∈ O_{X_{O_K}}(U) : x_K ∈ O^*_{X_K}(U_K)} for U an affine open, which holds also with self-intersections; hence M^gp(U) = O^*_{X_K}(U_K). With X_K := X_{O_K,K}, 𝔛 := X_{O_C} and X := X_{K,C}, the Hodge–Tate symbol maps r_HT : O(X_K)^{*,⊗i} → H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛), i ≥ 1, are defined by cup products of the Chern class maps c^{HT}_1 : τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1]) → Ω_𝔛[−1], x ↦ dlog(x) = dx/x.
items.note: The canonical-log-structure statement is the same one §7.2 of the companion paper uses, and it is an item of the roadmap proposed there; here it is the input that makes the Hodge–Tate Chern class a map out of the units of the generic fibre.

items.name: Proposition 3.3 and Lemma 3.4: the A_inf and Hodge–Tate symbols agree under the Hodge–Tate specialisation
items.statement: For i ≥ 1 the symbol maps r_inf and r_HT are compatible under the Hodge–Tate specialisation map ι_HT: ι_HT ∘ (r_inf|_{O(X_K)^{*,⊗i}}) = r_HT. For i = 1 (Lemma 3.4) the composition O(X_K)^* → O(X)^* ≅ H^1_ét(𝔛,τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1])) —c^{inf}_1→ H^1_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{1}) —ι_HT{1}→ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^1_𝔛) equals c^{HT}_1 = dlog. The case i ≥ 1 follows because the edge map in the local–global spectral sequence, the map θ̃ : AΩ_𝔛 → Ω̃_𝔛 (compatible with products since Lη is lax symmetric monoidal) and the isomorphism of Theorem 2.5 are all compatible with products.
items.note: This compatibility is what lets the Hodge–Tate reduction of the A_inf regulator be identified with the Hodge–Tate regulator of the companion paper, which is the pivot of the whole proof.

items.name: Scholze's isomorphism R^iν_{X,*}Ô(i) ≅ Ω^i_X and its characterisation by the Kummer map
items.statement: Scholze's isomorphism α_2 : R^1ν_{X,*}Ô(1) ≅ Ω^1_X is uniquely characterised by the property that its inverse is the unique O_X-linear map Ω^1_X → R^1ν_{X,*}Ô(1) making the square with dlog : O^*_X → Ω^1_X and c^{proét}_1 : O^*_X → R^1ν_{X,*}Ẑ_p(1) commute, and it extends to isomorphisms R^iν_{X,*}Ô(i) ≅ Ω^i_X for all i ≥ 0. Since coherent sheaves have no higher cohomology on affinoids (Tate acyclicity), the spectral sequence R^iε_*(R^jν_{X,*}Ô) ⇒ R^{i+j}ν_*Ô degenerates and gives R^1ν_*Ô(1) ≅ ε_*R^1ν_{X,*}Ô(1) ≅ ε_*Ω^1_𝔛, where ε : X_ét → 𝔛_ét.
items.note: P8 constructs the shared relative period sheaves from R06.1, AInfCohomology AI.3 and AdicEtaleGeometry, which is where Scholze's computation of R^iν_*Ô belongs; the companion extraction routed the same statement there.

items.name: The proof of Lemma 3.4: reduction to a small algebra and the comparison of α_1 with α_2
items.statement: One must show that ρ = ι, where ι : Ω^1_𝔛 → ε_*Ω^1_𝔛 is the natural (injective, as 𝔛 is flat over O_C) map inducing C ⊗_{O_C} Ω^1_𝔛 ≅ ε_*Ω^1_𝔛, and ρ is the composite Ω^1_𝔛 —α_1^{-1}→ H^1(Ω̃_𝔛{1}) —can→ R^1ν_*Ô^+{1} → R^1ν_*Ô(1) —α_2→ ε_*Ω^1_𝔛, with α_1 : H^1(Ω̃_𝔛{1}) ≅ Ω^1_𝔛 given by Theorem 2.5 and the middle map induced by Ô^+ ⊂ Ô and by O_C{1} → C(1), informally x{1} ↦ x/(ζ_p − 1)·(1), made rigorous by writing x{1} = xω with ω = dlog(ζ)/(ζ_p − 1). Both maps are O_𝔛-linear, so the claim is local and reduces, by functoriality, to a small algebra R with a framing O_C{T^{±1}_i} → R and then to R = A = O_C{T^{±1}}, where it follows from the construction of α_1: since can ∘ γ_2 is multiplication by ζ_p − 1, one has (ζ_p − 1)γ_2^{-1}(α_1^{-1}(dT/T)) = can(α_1^{-1}(dT/T)), which corresponds to the element (γ ↦ (ζ_p − 1) ⊗ (1/(ζ_p−1))dlog(ζ_γ)) of (ζ_p − 1)H^1(Γ,A_∞){1}, and the compatibility of α_2 with the Kummer map gives ρ(dT/T) = dT/T. One then checks that the composite O^*_X → R^1ν_{X,*}Ẑ_p(1) → R^1ν_{X,*}A_inf{1} —θ̃→ R^1ν_{X,*}Ô^+{1} → R^1ν_{X,*}Ô(1) → Ω^1_X is dlog, because on Ẑ_p(1) → A_inf{1} → Ô^+{1} → Ô(1) an element x(1) goes to μx{1}, then to θ̃(μx{1}) = (ζ_p − 1)x{1}, then to x(1); and assembles the large commutative diagram of the two Chern classes, the two specialisations and the edge maps.
items.note: The explicit computation with x{1} = xω and θ̃(μx{1}) = (ζ_p − 1)x{1} is the normalisation that makes the A_inf and Hodge–Tate symbols match; AI.0 fixes θ̃ = θ∘φ^{-1}, which is the convention used here.

items.name: Theorem 4.1: the A_inf-cohomology of the Drinfeld symmetric space
items.statement: Let i ≥ 0. There is a G × G_K-equivariant isomorphism of topological A_inf-modules A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^* ≅ H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}), compatible with the operator φ^{-1}, where 𝔛 = X_{O_K} ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C for the standard semistable model X_{O_K} of H^d_K, Sp^i(Z_p)^* is the continuous Z_p-dual of the generalized Steinberg representation, G acts by duality on it and trivially on A_inf, G_K acts on A_inf and on 𝔛, and the completed tensor product is taken in pro-discrete modules. The isomorphism is the A_inf-regulator r_inf of Corollary 4.13. Both sides vanish for i > d.
items.note: The technical heart of the paper, and the statement that Theorem 5.1 turns into the integral étale computation through the Artin–Schreier sequence.

items.name: Standard parabolics, the flag spaces X_J, the generalized Steinberg representations Sp_J(A) and the indexing Sp^r
items.statement: B ⊂ G = GL_{d+1}(K) is the upper triangular Borel and ∆ = {1,…,d} the set of simple roots; for J ⊆ ∆, P_J is the standard parabolic and X_J = G/P_J a compact (profinite) space, with surjections X_J → X_{J∪{i}}. For an abelian group A, Sp_J(A) := LC(X_J,A)/Σ_{i ∈ ∆∖J} LC(X_{J∪{i}},A), where LC(−,A) denotes locally constant A-valued functions (automatically compactly supported) and the subspaces are embedded by pullback; it is a smooth A[G]-module with Sp_J(A) ≅ Sp_J(Z) ⊗ A, Sp_∅ the usual Steinberg representation and Sp_∆(A) = A. One writes Sp^r := Sp_{{1,…,d−r}} for 0 ≤ r ≤ d and Sp^r = 0 for r > d, so that Sp^0(A) = A and Sp^d = Sp_∅.
items.note: The same representations as in the companion paper (where they are written Sp_r); this is the integral form, with Z_p and F_p coefficients, in which the answer of Theorem 1.1 is phrased. Nothing in the atlas builds them.

items.name: Theorem 4.3 (Grosse-Klönne) and the rigidity of the G-stable lattice
items.statement: If A is a field of characteristic p then the Sp_J(A), for varying J ⊆ ∆, are exactly the irreducible constituents of the smooth G-representation LC(G/B,A), each with multiplicity one; in particular each Sp_J(A) is irreducible. Two consequences are used to lift the rational computation of the companion paper to O_K: Sp^i(O_K) is, up to a K^*-homothety, the unique G-stable lattice in Sp^i(K), and Sp^i(k) — the reduction mod p of Sp^i(O_K) — is irreducible.
items.note: This rigidity is what makes an integral statement follow from a rational one: a G-stable lattice in Sp^i(K) is determined up to scaling, so the integral regulator is pinned down by its rational avatar.

items.name: Topologies on Sp_J(Λ) and on its continuous dual; compactness and torsion-freeness of Sp_J(O_L)^*
items.statement: For a topological ring Λ, writing the profinite X_J = lim←_n X_{n,J} with X_{n,J} finite gives LC(X_J,Λ) = lim→_n LC(X_{n,J},Λ) with each term finite free over Λ, hence an inductive-limit topology on LC(X_J,Λ) and a quotient topology on Sp_J(Λ). With M^* := Hom_cont(M,Λ) carrying the weak topology, LC(X_J,Λ)^* ≅ lim←_n LC(X_{n,J},Λ)^* is a countable inverse limit of finite free Λ-modules, and Sp_J(Λ)^* is the closed submodule of functionals killing Σ_{i ∈ ∆∖J} LC(X_{J∪{i}},Λ). For L/Q_p finite, Sp_J(O_L)^* is a compact torsion-free O_L-module.
items.note: Compactness and torsion-freeness of the dual are what make the domain of the regulator ξ̃-torsion free in §4.4, and they are why all the isomorphisms can be called topological. As printed, the displayed identification of the dual is of LC(X_J,Λ) rather than of the quotient Sp_J(Λ) — the same slip as in the companion paper.

items.name: Distributions on H^{i+1}, the harmonic non-degenerate cochains, and Sp^i(Z) ≅ LC_c(H^{i+1},Z)
items.statement: For a profinite set S and an abelian group A, D(S,A) := Hom(LC(S,Z),A) = LC(S,A)^* is the space of A-valued locally constant distributions; the Dirac distributions δ_x, δ_x(f) = f(x), span a dense submodule. For H ∈ H let ℓ_H be a unimodular equation (integral coefficients, at least one a unit), determined up to a unit of O_K, so that ℓ_{H′}/ℓ_H is an invertible analytic function on H^d_K. LC_c(H^{i+1},Z) is the space of locally constant f : H^{i+1} → Z such that Σ_{s=0}^{i+1} (−1)^s f(H_0,…,Ĥ_s,…,H_{i+1}) = 0 for all H_0,…,H_{i+1} (harmonicity) and f(H_0,…,H_i) = 0 whenever the ℓ_{H_j}, 0 ≤ j ≤ i, are linearly dependent (non-degeneracy). The work of Schneider–Stuhler gives a G-equivariant isomorphism Sp^i(Z) ≅ LC_c(H^{i+1},Z), so the inclusion LC_c ⊂ LC dualises to a strict exact sequence 0 → D(H^{i+1},A)_deg → D(H^{i+1},A) → Hom(Sp^i(Z),A) → 0 defining the degenerate distributions; it is split, all three modules being duals of free modules.
items.note: The splitness of (4.4) is what survives tensoring with A_inf, and it is the reason the regulator descends to the Steinberg dual after completion. The sentence introducing the isomorphism attaches the reference of the authors' own paper to "the work of Schneider–Stuhler"; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: Theorem 4.5 (Grosse-Klönne): acyclicity, the vanishing of d, and the splitting of the de Rham complex of the model
items.statement: For i > 0 and j ≥ 0, H^i_ét(X_{O_K},Ω^j_{X_{O_K}}) = 0, and the de Rham differential vanishes on H^0_ét(X_{O_K},Ω^j_{X_{O_K}}), where Ω^• is the logarithmic de Rham complex of the standard model over O_K for the canonical log structures. Consequently RΓ_dR(X_{O_K}) ≅ RΓ_ét(X_{O_K},Ω^•) ≅ ⊕_{i ≥ 0} Γ_ét(X_{O_K},Ω^i)[−i], so H^i_dR(X_{O_K}) ≅ H^0_ét(X_{O_K},Ω^i_{X_{O_K}}).
items.note: This is the pro-ordinarity input, and in §4.4 it is what kills the higher terms E_2^{s,t} = H^s_ét(𝔛,Ω^t{i−t}) = 0 for s ≥ 1 of the local–global spectral sequence, so that H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃) ≅ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛).

items.name: Theorem 4.6 and Corollary 4.7: the integral de Rham and Hodge–Tate regulators of the companion paper
items.statement: Let i ≥ 0. There are natural de Rham and Hodge–Tate regulator maps r_dR : D(H^{i+1},O_K) → H^i_dR(X_{O_K}) and r_HT : D(H^{i+1},O_K) → H^0(X_{O_K},Ω^i_{X_{O_K}}) which factor through Sp^i(O_K)^* and induce topological G-equivariant isomorphisms Sp^i(O_K)^* ≅ H^i_dR(X_{O_K}) and Sp^i(O_K)^* ≅ H^0(X_{O_K},Ω^i_{X_{O_K}}), compatibly through the isomorphism of Theorem 4.5. Their proof starts from the Schneider–Stuhler isomorphism Sp^i(K)^* ≅ H^i_dR(X_K), made explicit as a de Rham regulator on distributions by Iovita–Spiess, and lifts it to O_K using a detailed analysis of the integral Hyodo–Kato cohomology of the special fibre together with the rigidity of the G-stable lattice and the mod p irreducibility of Sp^i. Base changing (Corollary 4.7) gives topological G-equivariant isomorphisms r_dR : Sp^i(O_K)^* ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C ≅ H^i_dR(𝔛) and r_HT : Sp^i(O_K)^* ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C ≅ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛), i.e. r_HT : O_C ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^* ≅ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛).
items.locator: Theorem 4.6 with footnote 11 and Corollary 4.7, §4.2, p. 18 (quoted from the companion paper)
items.note: This is Theorem 6.26 of PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20, i.e. an item of the Drinfeld roadmap proposed by that extraction; the Hodge–Tate form is the single geometric input that makes the reduction of r_inf an isomorphism in §4.4.

items.name: The étale symbol function ψ_ét on H^{i+1} and its continuity
items.statement: Fix i ≥ 1 and set M := H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)). For H_0,…,H_i ∈ H put ψ_ét(H_0,…,H_i) := r_ét(ℓ_{H_1}/ℓ_{H_0} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ ℓ_{H_i}/ℓ_{H_0}) ∈ M, where r_ét is the i-fold cup product of the étale Chern class of §3; it is independent of the choice of unimodular equations. Continuity is proved over the standard admissible affinoid covering {U_n} of X, with Π(n) the profinite étale fundamental group of U_n: by Scholze's K(π,1)-theorem continuous Π(n)-cochains compute RΓ_ét(U_n,Z_p(i)), and since Π(n) acts trivially on Z_p(1) the local Chern class factors through Hom(Π(n),Z_p(1)). By continuity of the cup product one reduces to degree 1, i.e. to Ψ_{1,n} : H^2 → Hom(Π(n),Z_p(1)) =: M_n, and then to showing that for every k there is m such that m-equivalent hyperplanes H_0, H_1 — those admitting unimodular equations congruent modulo ϖ^m — satisfy r_ét(ℓ_{H_1}/ℓ_{H_0}) ∈ p^k M_n; this holds because for m large ℓ_{H_1}/ℓ_{H_0} has a p^{r_n m}-th root in O(U_n)^* for a constant r_n depending only on U_n, and r_ét is a homomorphism.
items.note: The m-equivalence filtration H = lim←_m H_m of the profinite set of hyperplanes is what converts "the symbol map is continuous" into a statement about p-divisibility of ratios of unimodular equations; it is the technical heart of the integration.

items.name: Proposition 4.8: the étale symbols integrate against distributions and factor through the Steinberg dual
items.statement: Let i ≥ 1. (1) There is a unique continuous Z_p-linear map r_ét : D(H^{i+1},Z_p) → H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) with r_ét(δ_{(H_0,…,H_i)}) = ψ_ét(H_0,…,H_i) for all H_0,…,H_i; uniqueness because the Dirac distributions span a dense submodule, existence by integrating the continuous map Ψ_{i,n} against distributions into the p-adically complete target and taking the limit r_ét := lim←_n r_ét,n. (2) This map factors through Sp^i(Z_p)^* and induces r_ét : Sp^i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)). The factorisation is proved by verifying the two conditions defining LC_c(H^{i+1},Z) for ψ_ét: the alternating-sum relation, obtained by writing ℓ_{H_j}/ℓ_{H_1} = (ℓ_{H_j}/ℓ_{H_0})(ℓ_{H_0}/ℓ_{H_1}), expanding multiplicatively and using that r_ét is alternating so that all terms with two factors ℓ_{H_0}/ℓ_{H_1} die; and the vanishing on linearly dependent tuples, which follows from the Steinberg relations.
items.note: The étale regulator of this proposition is the map the whole paper is built on: r_inf is γ ∘ r_ét, and Theorem 5.1 is the statement that r_ét itself is an isomorphism.

items.name: The vanishing of degenerate symbols: Steinberg relations in Milnor K-theory and the two-step reduction
items.statement: If the ℓ_{H_j}, 0 ≤ j ≤ i, are linearly dependent then ψ_ét(H_0,…,H_i) = 0, because the étale regulator satisfies the Steinberg relations. Precisely, with x_j = ℓ_j/ℓ_0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ i it suffices to show that the symbol {x_1,…,x_i,1 + a_1x_1 + ⋯ + a_ix_i} vanishes in the Milnor K-theory group K^M_{i+1}(O(X)) for a_j ∈ K, knowing that {x_1,…,x_i,1} = 0. Reordering so that y_1 := 1 + a_1x_1 ≠ 0 and using {z,1−z} = 0 and {x,a} = 0 for a ∈ K^*, one computes {x_1,x_2,…,x_i,1 + a_1x_1 + ⋯ + a_ix_i} = {x_1,x_2/y_1,…,x_i/y_1,1 + a_2x_2/y_1 + ⋯ + a_ix_i/y_1}, which makes sense because x_j/y_1 = ℓ_j/(ℓ_0 + a_1ℓ_1) is again a ratio of linear equations of K-rational hyperplanes, hence a unit on X; repeating i times reduces the last entry to 1.
items.note: That the intermediate quotients ℓ_j/(ℓ_0 + a_1ℓ_1) are again ratios of hyperplane equations is what keeps the reduction inside the units of the space; as printed the range of j in x_j = ℓ_j/ℓ_0 starts at 0, and the Milnor K-group is written of O(X)^* rather than of O(X) — both recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The A_inf-regulator r_inf := γ ∘ r_ét and its A_inf-linear extension (Corollary 4.13)
items.statement: For i ≥ 1 define r_inf : D(H^{i+1},Z_p) → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) and r_inf : Sp^i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) as γ ∘ r_ét, where γ : H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) comes from Theorem 2.9 and lands in the φ^{-1}-fixed part. Corollary 4.13: these extend uniquely to compatible continuous A_inf-linear maps r_inf : A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} D(H^{i+1},Z_p) → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) and r_inf : A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}), compatible with the étale regulators. Uniqueness is clear from A_inf-linearity and density; for existence one works over the covering, sets r_inf,n := γ r_ét,n into RΓ_ét(𝔘_n,AΩ_{𝔘_n}{i})[i], notes that r_ét,n factors through a module M_n of continuous Π(n)-cochains, and composes A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} D(H^{i+1},Z_p) → A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} lim←_n M_n ≅ lim←_n(A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} M_n) → holim_n RΓ_ét(𝔘_n,AΩ_{𝔘_n}{i})[i] ≅ RΓ_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})[i], the third map existing because both sides are derived (p,μ)-adically complete. The descent to the Steinberg dual uses that (4.4) stays strict exact after ⊗̂A_inf, which holds because it is split.
items.note: The only delicate point is the strict surjectivity after completion, which is why the splitness of (4.4) is recorded. As printed, the module M_n is described as Hom(Π(n),Z_p(i)) although the regulator has degree i; recorded in sourceIssues.

items.name: The proof of Theorem 4.1: φ^{-1}-compatibility, the reduction modulo ξ̃, ξ̃-torsion-freeness and derived Nakayama
items.statement: For i = 0 both sides of (4.2) are A_inf, so one may assume i ≥ 1. The map r_inf is φ^{-1}-compatible because it is A_inf-linear and induced from r_ét, hence lands in the φ^{-1}-fixed part. Its reduction r̄_inf : (A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^*)/ξ̃ → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})/ξ̃ is a topological isomorphism: it fits in a commutative diagram whose left vertical θ̃ : (A_inf ⊗̂ Sp^i(Z_p)^*)/ξ̃ ≅ O_C ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp^i(Z_p)^* is an isomorphism since ker θ̃ = (ξ̃), whose right vertical α : H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})/ξ̃ → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃) is the injective change-of-coefficients map, whose lower right vertical is the isomorphism H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃) ≅ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛) coming from H^t(AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃) ≅ H^t(Ω̃_𝔛{i}) ≅ Ω^t_𝔛{i−t} (Theorems 2.8 and 2.5) together with the vanishing of E_2^{s,t} for s ≥ 1 (Theorem 4.5), whose slanted arrows are the Hodge–Tate specialisation ι_HT and the Hodge–Tate regulator r_HT of Corollary 4.7, and which commutes by Proposition 3.3; it follows that α is surjective, hence an isomorphism, hence so is r̄_inf. The triangle AΩ_𝔛{i} —ξ̃→ AΩ_𝔛{i} → AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃ then gives 0 → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})/ξ̃ —α→ H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}/ξ̃) → H^{i+1}_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})[ξ̃] → 0, so H^{i+1}_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i})[ξ̃] = 0 and, i being arbitrary, H^j_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) is ξ̃-torsion free for all i,j. Hence the derived and naive reductions of r_inf agree, the homotopy fibre T of r_inf satisfies T ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_inf/ξ̃ ≅ 0, and T is derived ξ̃-complete (the domain is, and the target is by Theorem 2.8(3) together with the preservation of derived completeness by derived pushforward and by passage to cohomology); by derived Nakayama T ≅ 0, so r_inf is an isomorphism, and a topological one because θ̃ and ι_HT are.
items.note: This is the argument the introduction summarises: derived Nakayama plus a torsion-freeness statement replaces the perfectness arguments that properness would supply. The slanted arrow of the diagram is labelled ι_HK rather than ι_HT, and the middle term of the displayed exact sequence loses its twist; both recorded in sourceIssues.

routes.title: Drinfeld symmetric spaces, generalized Steinberg representations and their p-adic cohomology
routes.reason: This is the roadmap proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20 for the Drinfeld symmetric space H^d_K, its standard semistable model with the Bruhat–Tits combinatorics, the generalized Steinberg representations in their smooth, continuous and locally analytic forms, and the computation of the space's p-adic cohomology. The present paper is the integral refinement of exactly that computation — it replaces Q_p-coefficients by Z_p and F_p — and it reuses the same objects: the standard model, Grosse-Klönne's acyclicity of the sheaves of logarithmic differentials, the integral de Rham cohomology of the model, the rigidity of G-stable lattices in Sp_i(Q_p), and the measure-theoretic description of Sp_i(Z_p)^* with its regulators. So the results of §§4–5 and the main theorems of §1 join that roadmap rather than opening a second one; what is genuinely new machinery — the A_inf symbol maps and the handling of a non-proper space — is the Part II below.
routes.brief: Add to the roadmap proposed by PAPER-COLMEZ-DOSPINESCU-NIZIOL-20 the integral refinement of its main computation. Final theorems, as this paper states them. (1) Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 5.1: for i ≥ 0, G × G_K-equivariant topological isomorphisms H^i_ét(H^d_C,Z_p(i)) ≅ Sp_i(Z_p)^* and H^i_ét(H^d_C,F_p(i)) ≅ Sp_i(F_p)^*, compatible with the rational isomorphism of the companion paper; in particular the integral cohomology is p-torsion free and both vanish for i > d. (2) Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 4.1: a topological φ^{-1}-equivariant isomorphism of G × G_K-modules H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) ≅ A_inf ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp_i(Z_p)^*, where 𝔛 = X_{O_K} ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C for the standard semistable model X_{O_K} of H^d_K. (3) The integral representation theory that the answer is phrased in: the generalized Steinberg representations Sp_i(Z_p) and Sp_i(F_p) with their duals as pro-discrete modules, their topologies and compactness, the rigidity of G-stable lattices and the mod p irreducibility (Grosse-Klönne), and the interpretation of Sp_i(Z_p)^* as a quotient of the space of Z_p-valued measures on H^{i+1} after Schneider–Stuhler and Iovita–Spiess, with the Dirac distributions and the uniqueness of the extension of a regulator from them. (4) The integral de Rham input: Grosse-Klönne's acyclicity H^i(X_{O_K},Ω^j) = 0 for i ≥ 1, the ordinarity of the standard model, the companion paper's computation of the integral de Rham cohomology of the model and of the Hodge–Tate regulator r_HT : O_C ⊗̂_{Z_p} Sp_i(Z_p)^* ≅ H^0_ét(𝔛,Ω^i_𝔛). (5) The assembly: the étale regulator r_ét : Sp_i(Z_p)^* → H^i_ét(X,Z_p(i)) obtained by integrating étale symbols, the derived Nakayama argument reducing Theorem 4.1 to its Hodge–Tate reduction, the ξ̃-torsion-freeness of both sides, and the deduction of Theorem 5.1 from the twisted Artin–Schreier sequence together with A_inf^{φ^{-1}=1} = Z_p and A_inf{1}/(1−φ^{-1}) = 0. Import the A_inf-cohomology package from AInfCohomology AI.0–AI.6 and the nearby-cycle formula from PrismaticCohomology PR.4, and the A_inf symbol maps from the Part II below. Do not plan the compactly supported computation or any Poincaré duality for these spaces: the paper states that no such duality is known and that basic examples show there is no naive one.

routes.title: A_inf-cohomology, Part II: symbol maps and non-proper spaces
routes.reason: AInfCohomology builds the A_inf-cohomology of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze: the period rings and twists (AI.0), the décalage operator (AI.1), AΩ = Lη_μ Rν_* A_inf,X on the pro-étale site (AI.3), the Hodge–Tate and crystalline specialisations (AI.4), the proper theory with its torsion control (AI.5) and the semistable extension of Česnavičius–Koshikawa (AI.6). Two things this paper needs are new layers in that direction rather than a new roadmap. First, Chern classes and symbol maps with values in AΩ: the pro-étale Chern class from the Kummer sequence, the twisted Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism Ẑ_p(1) ≅ [A_inf{1} → A_inf{1}] that turns it into an A_inf-symbol, and the proof that this symbol is compatible with the Hodge–Tate one under the specialisation of AI.4 — nothing in AI.0–AI.7 mentions Chern classes. Second, the theory beyond properness: AI.5 and AI.6 are stated for proper (formal) models, and the paper's whole point is that the A_inf-cohomology and the nearby-cycle formula make sense without properness, so that ξ̃-torsion-freeness and derived Nakayama can replace the perfectness arguments that properness supplies.
routes.brief: Final theorems, as the paper states them. (1) The symbol maps: for X a smooth adic space over C with a flat p-adic formal model 𝔛 over O_C and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét, construct compatible continuous maps r_proét : O(X)^{*,⊗i} → H^i_proét(X,Ẑ_p(i)) and r_inf : O(X)^{*,⊗i} → H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) for i ≥ 1, from the sheaf-level Chern classes c^{proét}_1 : τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1]) → τ^{≤1}Rν_*Ẑ_p(1) and c^{inf}_1 : τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1]) → τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1} together with the identification H^1_ét(𝔛,τ^{≤1}(Rν_*G_m[−1])) ≅ O(X)^*, and by cup products in higher degrees. (2) The two inputs to c^{inf}_1: the Kummer exact sequence 0 → Ẑ_p(1) → lim←_{x↦x^p} G_m → G_m → 0 on the pro-étale site, obtained from the finite-level Kummer sequences and the vanishing of R^1 lim, and the twisted Artin–Schreier quasi-isomorphism Ẑ_p(1) ≅ [A_inf{1} —1−φ^{-1}→ A_inf{1}], x(1) ↦ μx{1}; prove that the resulting map to τ^{≤1}AΩ_𝔛{1} is compatible with the map to τ^{≤1}Rν_*A_inf{1} and that its composite with 1 − φ^{-1} vanishes, so that symbols land in the φ^{-1}-fixed part. (3) The Hodge–Tate compatibility (Proposition 3.3 and Lemma 3.4): ι_HT ∘ r_inf = r_HT on units of the generic fibre, where r_HT is built from c^{HT}_1 = dlog; the proof needs Scholze's characterisation of R^1ν_{X,*}Ô(1) ≅ Ω^1_X by the Kummer map and the explicit normalisation x{1} = xω with ω = dlog(ζ)/(ζ_p − 1), under which θ̃(μx{1}) = (ζ_p − 1)x{1}, the O_𝔛-linearity of both comparisons, the reduction to a small framed algebra O_C{T^{±1}}, and the compatibility of the edge maps of the local–global spectral sequences and of θ̃ : AΩ_𝔛 → Ω̃_𝔛 with products, the latter because Lη is lax symmetric monoidal. (4) The non-proper package: prove that derived ξ̃-completeness of both sides plus the derived Nakayama lemma reduces an isomorphism of A_inf-cohomologies to its reduction modulo ξ̃; prove the ξ̃-torsion-freeness of H^i_ét(𝔛,AΩ_𝔛{i}) from the long exact sequences of the specialisation, so that the naive reduction agrees with the derived one; and record which statements of AI.5 and AI.6 (perfectness, BKF conditions, finiteness) are unavailable because 𝔛 is not quasi-compact. Import the period rings and twists from AI.0, the décalage operator and its lax monoidality from AI.1, AΩ and the pro-étale period sheaves from AI.3, the Hodge–Tate specialisation from AI.4, the semistable and logarithmic versions from AI.6, the nearby-cycle formula from PrismaticCohomology PR.4, and Scholze's computation of R^iν_*Ô from PadicHodgeTheory P8. Do not plan the Drinfeld computation here: it is the roadmap above.

That is precisely the content of §2 of this paper, which quotes Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze and Česnavičius–Koshikawa verbatim. The paper is a consumer; what it adds — symbols, and the theory without properness — is the Part II above.

PR.4 owns the étale comparison and the p-adic Tate twists, and names BMS2 §10 among its sources with the instruction to prove the truncation and nearby-cycle comparisons under those hypotheses; the extraction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19 routes its chapter-10 items (the fixed points of ξ^iφ^{-1} on A_inf,X, the Lη_μ fixed points, the vanishing of the syntomic complexes above the twist) to the same stage. A1 builds the small étale and pro-étale sites of an adic space, with Scholze's corrected covering definition and the geometric points and stalks; the sheaf Ẑ_p = lim_n Z/p^n on X_proét, the failure of repleteness of that site and the vanishing of the derived limits R^i lim_n Z/p^n (Scholze, Prop. 8.2) belong with it. gaps.detail: Remark 1.2(iii) observes that the computation of this paper and the compactly supported computation of Colmez–Dospinescu–Hauseux–Nizioł put étale and compactly supported étale cohomology of H^d_C in an abstract duality H^i_{ét,c}(H^d_C,Z/p^n) ≅ H^{2d−i}_ét(H^d_C,Z/p^n)^*(−d), but that there is no known Poincaré duality for spaces like H^d_C that would explain it or let one deduce one computation from the other, and that computations with basic analytic spaces such as the unit ball show that there is no naive Poincaré duality for general p-adic rigid analytic spaces. A design job must not plan such a duality, and must not plan either computation as a consequence of the other.

The integral comparison theorems that would give the result immediately — Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze as extended by Česnavičius–Koshikawa, to the effect that p-torsion freeness of the de Rham cohomology of a proper semistable model implies p-torsion freeness of the p-adic étale cohomology of the generic fibre — are proved using properness, and the paper says it is not clear how to adapt them; the standard model of H^d_K is not even quasi-compact. So AInfCohomology AI.5 and AI.6, which are stated for proper models, cannot be quoted for this geometry, and what replaces them here is the combination of the nearby-cycle formula (which needs no quasi-compactness), derived ξ̃-completeness and a hand-proved ξ̃-torsion-freeness. A layer must not assume the proper statements apply.

The paper records that the syntomic method of the companion paper "works well only up to some absolute constants", which is why that paper obtained only the rational answer, and that this is what forced the passage to A_inf-cohomology. The two routes are therefore not interchangeable: the syntomic one gives the rational computation and the p-torsion freeness of the integral de Rham cohomology, the A_inf one the integral étale answer.

Theorem 2.9 is quoted from Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze's chapter 10, where it is proved in the good reduction case; §2.4 of this paper shows that the proof goes through for an arbitrary flat formal model. A design job importing the formula from PrismaticCohomology PR.4 must therefore also carry that extension, which is why it is routed with the Part II rather than as a planned item.

The subscript c in LC_c(H^{i+1},Z) is never explained, and it cannot mean compact support, since §4.1.1 notes that locally constant functions on these compact spaces automatically have compact support; it abbreviates the two conditions imposed in the preceding display (harmonicity and vanishing on linearly dependent tuples). A formalisation should take those two conditions as the definition.
